Definition: from G3844 and the base of G1927; an alien alongside, i.e. a resident foreigner:--pilgrim, stranger.
BiblicalUsage: Parepidemos is a pilgrim, a resident foreigner, an alien alongside. Peter addresses the strangers scattered through Pontus and Asia in 1 Peter 1:1, and in 1 Peter 2:11 he calls them dearly beloved strangers and pilgrims, and begs them to abstain from fleshly lusts. Hebrews 11:13 says the patriarchs confessed that they were strangers and pilgrims on the earth.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe a pilgrim is not lost, he is on his way, and the confession of Hebrews is the one I want to make: I am a stranger here because my country is somewhere else. That is why I hold that the Christian life is lived with a packed bag and an open heart.
